title: Focus management and live-announcements playbook for dynamic panels
content:
Summary:
This playbook captures UX notes, wireframe annotations, and a prioritized backlog for improving focus management and screen reader announcements across dynamic panels in the Console (Model Inspector, Routing, and Live Logs). The goal is to provide a consistent, predictable keyboard and AT experience for users interacting with asynchronous content and frequently-updated controls.

Context and motivation:
- Console has several dynamic panels that update in-place (model routing, live request logs, streaming output preview).
- Current problems surfaced in usability testing and CS tickets: focus loss when panels update, missing or noisy announcements for background updates, and inconsistent return-focus after closing panels.
- Fixing these helps power users (keyboard-first engineers, SREs) and customers using assistive tech. It also reduces support tickets for perceived instability.

High-level goals:
1) Ensure every transient panel/modal preserves and restores focus predictably.
2) Announce important state changes (errors, completion of long-running tasks, routing fallback) without overwhelming users.
3) Provide a reference keyboard flow for each panel and component; include acceptance criteria and example ARIA patterns.

Observed issues (short list from recent testing and logs):
- Model Inspector: when model metadata finishes loading, focus jumps to the panel body and screen readers read the whole block; users lose their place.
- Routing Rules editor: adding a new rule inserts a field and focus lands inconsistently (sometimes on the top of list).
- Streaming Preview: interim tokens cause frequent aria-live updates; NVDA/VoiceOver repeat the same phrase multiple times.
- Snapshots modal: close button is not in tab order for some keyboard users due to a JS re-render.
- Toasts and inline banners: no clear role or aria-live policy; sometimes critical error toasts are announced as polite.

Wireframe / component-level notes (annotated behaviors to implement):
1) Model Inspector panel (right-side slide-over)
   - Wireframe: header with title, model selector, save/close controls; body with metadata sections (tabs), logs and performance metrics card.
   - Focus model: open => focus set to panel title (h2) or first interactive control depending on entry point. Close => return focus to the element that launched the panel.
   - ARIA: panel role="dialog" aria-modal="false" (since console allows background keyboard access) and aria-label="Model inspector for <model-name>". If opened from a keyboard action, set focus to the first form control; if opened from a mouse, set focus to title.
   - Announcements: when metadata load completes, use an offscreen status element aria-live="polite" with short message: "Model details loaded." Avoid pushing full table content.

2) Routing Rules editor (inline expandable section)
   - Wireframe: inline list of rules with add/remove, drag handle, test button.
   - Focus model: after Add Rule, move focus to the new rule's first input and announce "New rule added."
   - ARIA: new rule container gets aria-live="assertive" only for the single short phrase. Avoid multiple assertive updates in a quick burst.

3) Streaming output preview (bottom dock)
   - Wireframe: collapsed state with last token count, expanded with streaming area and pause button.
   - Focus model: streaming should not steal focus from the editor. Provide a "View stream" button that moves focus into the stream area.
   - Announcements: use aria-live="polite" on a summary line ("Stream updated: +12 tokens"). Provide user preference to disable live updates for screen readers in profile settings.

4) Snapshot / modal flows
   - Wireframe: modal with snapshot name, timestamp, and actions.
   - Focus model: implement focus trap while modal is open. Set initial focus to the modal heading and restore to trigger on close. Ensure close button is first tabbable control for quick escape.

ARIA patterns and examples (developer-friendly snippets):
- Use `aria-describedby` to point to a brief load state message element instead of dumping entire contents into the live region.
- For critical errors: aria-live="assertive" and role="alert" for toasts that require immediate attention. Lower-priority info: aria-live="polite".
- For panels that update frequently, maintain a single small status element that is updated rather than altering multiple parts of the DOM.

Keyboard flow sequences (keystroke => expected):
- Open Model Inspector via keyboard (Enter on row) => focus to panel title; screen reader: "Model inspector: my-model-name".
- Tab through: Title -> Model selector -> Actions -> First metadata accordion.
- Accordion expanded via Space/Enter => focus moves to first control inside accordion.
- Close (Escape) => focus returns to originating row.
- Add Routing Rule (keyboard): focus on Add button -> press Enter -> focus moves to new rule input, SR reads "New rule added. Name field".

Microcopy guidance (short examples to include in components):
- Add button tooltip: "Add rule — opens a new routing rule row and moves focus to the name field."
- Streaming summary: "Stream updated: +{n} tokens (press Shift+S to focus)."
- Modal close aria-label: "Close snapshot dialog" rather than just "Close".

Backlog grooming (prioritized):
- BM-1: Model Inspector: preserve/restore focus and polite load announcement. Priority: P0. Assignee: Ethan Morales. Estimate: 5d. Acceptance criteria: opening via keyboard moves focus to panel title; closing returns focus to origin; screen reader hears only "Model details loaded" when content arrives.
- BM-2: Routing Rules: deterministic focus after Add/Remove and drag reordering. Priority: P1. Assignee: Priya Nair. Estimate: 3d. Acceptance criteria: new rule keyboard focus, SR says "New rule added"; removing rule moves focus to next logical element.
- BM-3: Streaming Preview: add opt-out toggle for live SR updates and implement summary-only aria-live updates. Priority: P1. Assignee: Morgan Lee. Estimate: 4d. Acceptance criteria: users can disable live updates; when enabled, SR hears short summaries only.
- BM-4: Toasts and banners: normalize aria-live roles (errors=assertive). Priority: P2. Assignee: Design System. Estimate: 2d.
- BM-5: Modal focus trap audit across console (sweep). Priority: P2. Assignee: SRE/UX pairing. Estimate: 3d.

Testing notes / acceptance steps for QA:
- Manual: VoiceOver (macOS), NVDA (Windows) and ChromeVox test for each flow. Test with slow and fast network conditions to reproduce streaming frequency.
- Automation: add basic Axe snapshots for DOM role expectations and a tiny e2e keyboard script that checks focus index order on opening and closing.

Open questions & tradeoffs:
- Should some dynamic summaries be configurable per org or user? (pref for user-level toggle so team docs/observability doesn't change for everyone)
- For panel role: dialog vs region — current leaning is role="dialog" with aria-modal="false" because background keyboard focus is needed for some workflows.

Next steps (short-term roadmap):
- Align with Design System on a shared FocusUtilities mixin and a small set of status elements (1 week).
- Implement BM-1 and BM-2 as a paired engineer/UX effort (sprint).
- Publish a 1-page Console A11y checklist that includes these patterns and link to the decision log.

Decision log reference: CONFLUENCE-DEV-10234 (contains previous a11y debates and testing artifacts).

Notes to reviewers: please flag any scenario where preserving background keyboard access would conflict with modal semantics for your component. If you have a component that currently re-renders its close button (causing tab order issues), add its path to JIRA-UI-8887 so we can sweep implementation details.
